Nothing else: the stand-in signs in only the people it lists, each admin has the same authenticator secret (e2e/fixtures/totp.mjs), and the app's sign-in is not touched.

Add two setups after the existing ones, each modelled on the one beside it. (1) setup('the Norwegian owner signs in'): with testDb(): if no store has the slug E2E_STORE_NB, insert an access request (email OWNER_NB.email, name OWNER_NB.name, store_name 'E2E Butikk') and call commerce.approve_access_request(request.id, E2E_STORE_NB, 'E2E Butikk', null), exactly as the owner's setup does for E2E_STORE; set setup_completed_at as that setup does. Sign in with the file's signIn(page, OWNER_NB.email, `/admin/${E2E_STORE_NB}`) (the form is in English: a new account's language is taken from the browser, which is English here), expect the h1 to be visible, save the state to OWNER_NB.state. THEN run: update commerce.accounts set admin_locale = 'nb-NO' where lower(email) = OWNER_NB.email. Then open `/admin/${E2E_STORE_NB}` again in the same context and expect page.locator('html') toHaveAttribute('lang', 'nb'); save the state again. (2) setup('the Norwegian platform admin signs in with the second step'): copy the first setup of the file (insert the account with platform_admin true, sign in with the password, the two-step page, totp(), wait for /admin/platform), with ADMIN_NB; save ADMIN_NB.state; then set admin_locale = 'nb-NO' for it and check <html lang="nb"> on /admin/platform the same way. Import the three new names. Both setups must hold on a fresh database and on one they ran against before (use 'on conflict do nothing' and 'where not exists' as the file does).

commits.title: Five signed-in screens in English and Norwegian: document, words handed and script by idle, against a baseline that only falls

changes.how: Keep the file's BUDGETS table and its tests as they are. Add below them a second describe, 'what a signed-in screen is handed'. SCREENS = five entries { key, path(store) } : 'home' -> `/admin/${store}`; 'orders' -> `/admin/${store}/orders`; 'product' -> `/admin/${store}/products/${id of the store's first product by created_at}` (select p.id from commerce.products p join commerce.stores s on s.id = p.store_id where s.slug = store order by p.created_at limit 1); 'builder' -> `/admin/${store}/pages/${id of the store's first page of type 'page'}` (the query the file already has); 'platform' -> '/admin/platform'. PEOPLE = { en: { owner: OWNER, admin: ADMIN, store: E2E_STORE }, nb: { owner: OWNER_NB, admin: ADMIN_NB, store: E2E_STORE_NB } }. For each language and each screen one test that opens a context with browser.newContext({ storageState: <owner's state, or the admin's for 'platform'> }) and measures three numbers. (1) document: html = text of context.request.get(address); html.length. (2) handed: the bytes of interface words in the document. Decode the payload: for every inline script whose text starts with 'self.__next_f.push(' take its argument with JSON.parse (the text between the first '(' and the last ')' is a JSON array such as [1,"..."]) and join the strings at index 1; in the joined text find every occurrence of '"texts":{' and, from its opening brace, take the balanced JSON object (count braces, skipping string contents and escaped quotes); handed = the sum of Buffer.byteLength of those objects. If the joined text holds no '"texts":{' on the store home, the words travel under another prop name: read src/components/admin/admin-areas.tsx and src/components/admin/admin-text-context.tsx, use the prop name AdminTextProvider is given, and say so in a comment. Also keep areas = the sorted top-level keys of those objects. (3) scriptByIdle: open a page in the context, collect in a 'response' handler every response whose request().resourceType() is 'script' (sum of (await response.body()).length, each URL once), go to the address with waitUntil 'load', then wait until no request has started or finished for 3,000 ms (poll every 250 ms; fail after 30 s with the last five addresses), and sum. For the nb tests also expect html to contain '<html lang="nb"'. The baseline: import baseline from './admin-handed.baseline.json'. When process.env.E2E_MEASURE === '1' print one line `[handed] ${lang} ${key} ${document} ${handed} ${scriptByIdle} ${areas.join(',')}` and do not assert. Else expect document <= baseline[lang][key].document * 1.02, handed <= baseline[lang][key].handed (exact ceiling: words are not noise), and scriptByIdle <= baseline[lang][key].scriptByIdle * 1.02, each with a message that names the screen, the language, both figures and 'lower the baseline in the same change when a figure falls: E2E_MEASURE=1 prints them'. Add one more test per language, 'the baseline is as low as the screens': fails when any measured figure is more than 5% under its baseline ('write the lower figure into admin-handed.baseline.json').

Shape: { "en": { "home": { "document": n, "handed": n, "scriptByIdle": n, "named": n, "areas": ["common", ...] }, "orders": {...}, "product": {...}, "builder": {...}, "platform": {...} }, "nb": { the same five }, "saves": {} }. Fill document, handed, scriptByIdle and areas from one E2E_MEASURE=1 run of the spec on the signed-in build. Fill named from node docs/audits/bloat-review-2026-11/scripts/handed.mjs (step 0.1): it prints per screen the words handed and the words the screen's parts name; take the 'named' figure for the route of each of the five screens (/admin/[store], /admin/[store]/orders, /admin/[store]/products/[productId], /admin/[store]/pages/[pageId], /admin/platform), in English and in Norwegian if the script prints both, else the same figure for both with a comment in the decision. named is a record, not asserted by the spec: the scan of every hand-down site is another step's. For orientation, on the review's build an English store home's document was 166,109 bytes and the orders list's 164,140.

commits.title: Record what a save answers with on the product editor and the builder

changes.how: Add a describe 'what a save answers with', English owner only, two tests. Each opens the screen (the product editor and the builder, addresses as above), makes the smallest real change, saves, and measures the response to the server action: listen with page.waitForResponse((r) => r.request().method() === 'POST' && r.request().headers()['next-action'] !== undefined) started before the press; answer = (await response.body()).length. Product editor: read how an existing signed-in spec changes and saves a product (rg -n 'getByRole\("button", \{ name: "Save' e2e/signed-in/products-grid.spec.ts e2e/signed-in/variants-scale.spec.ts e2e/signed-in/unit-price-editor.spec.ts) and do the same: append one character to the product's title field, press Save, wait for the answer, then set the title back and save again so the store is left as it was. Builder: read e2e/signed-in/builder-saved-edit.spec.ts for how a page is edited and saved; change one heading's text by one character, save, measure, undo and save. When E2E_MEASURE=1 print `[save] product ${answer}` and `[save] builder ${answer}`; else expect answer <= baseline.saves.product * 1.02 and the same for builder. If a save makes more than one action request, take the largest and say so in a comment.
Fill "saves": { "product": n, "builder": n } from the E2E_MEASURE=1 run.

stop_if: After admin_locale is set, the page's <html lang> is still 'en' for the Norwegian account: the language is cached somewhere per session. Report what you see; do not sign in again through a Norwegian form by guessing labels.

executor_why: Each test is specified, but reading the words out of the page's payload and timing a save's answer are easy to get subtly wrong, so a stronger model should read the measuring code and the first figures before the push.
